agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Diffusion factors peer evidence and bounded timing implications

analytical_question: What diffusion evidence and factors inform timing for this application and organization without deciding adoption?
general_et_finding: General generative-AI work-use evidence remains unchanged: substantial, heterogeneous and not a universal Rogers stage. It measures no installed base for autonomous technical-claim publication, so high tool uptake cannot establish diffusion of this application.
application_finding: Relative advantage is unknown and possible error costs are unmeasured. Compatibility is poor with the stated final-human-review workflow. Complexity increases through technical verification and exception handling. Trialability is weak for live automatic publishing, though a nonpublishing simulation could be reversible. Observability of polished output is insufficient: unsupported claims may escape visible design checks. These are scenario-specific inferences.
organization_specific_finding: The same hypothetical fast follower now considers removal of human approval. That application change increases the evidence needed before inferring useful timing. Technical reviewers and source owners remain necessary complements; diffusion data cannot substitute for them. No trusted opinion leader or relevant publication-safety standard is established.

evidence.claim: Defined-population work-use data do not measure complete workflow deployment.
evidence.date_or_recency: Published/updated Series updated 2026-10-20 10:40 AM CDT; observed Q2 2026 and Q3 2026; accessed 2026-10-26
evidence.notes: US employed adults aged 18 to 64; RPS nationally representative online labor-market survey | Share reporting generative AI use for their job; quarterly, not seasonally adjusted. | Self report, not installed business workflows; no inference of a durable reversal from one quarter without uncertainty analysis.

evidence.claim: The note explains why business and individual survey rates differ.
evidence.date_or_recency: Published/updated 2026-04-03; observed Through 2025; see source for survey-specific windows; accessed 2026-10-26
evidence.evidence_type: Official analysis or original researcher account
evidence.notes: Compares firms, individual workers and workforce-weighted exposure | Different samples and units of analysis | Used for measurement interpretation, not the latest October 2026 prevalence.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: No matched adoption evidence exists for this autonomous use.
A favorable attribute of a reviewed drafting tool cannot be transferred to automatic publication.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence in the qualitative broad signal; low in autonomous application spread and value. Control incompatibility follows directly from the case change.
value_opportunity_implication: No net benefit or diffusion-based timing advantage is established.
risk_governance_implication: Refer technical-claim verification, human authority and consequences to risk/readiness owners; do not infer acceptable risk from widespread AI use.
recommendation_management_implication: Diffusion evidence supplies no justification for live automatic-publication timing. Limit any proposed learning to a separately approved nonpublishing simulation and hand the operational decision to the Adoption Agent.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reassess only after appropriate application evidence, approval architecture and independent technical controls are established.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Withhold autonomous application stage and adoption permission.
Need specific comparable workflows and evidence on technical verification and publication controls.
